title: Secondleg they should be.
html_source:
The brutish and obnoxious Mulligan, although treated with mockery and even contempt in Ulysses, still shares with its author a keen poetic sensibility. Here, specifically, he demonstrates a fondness for puns and an awareness of the myriad minor absurdities built into the English language.

Note the rhythmic similarity between the narrator’s adverb (“contentedly”) and the character’s dialogue (“secondleg they should be”).

anchor.prefix:
How are the secondhand breeks? 

 — They fit well enough, Stephen answered. 

 Buck Mulligan attacked the hollow beneath his underlip. 

 — The mockery of it, he said contentedly.
